object_description: compact angular sports center with stacked and partly underground volumes
design_condition: The compact sports center is relocated to the park's northwest edge and stacks its uses to preserve the largest possible contiguous open space, while the deep basement and roof structures intensify its technical and operational demands.

positive.statement: The peripheral compact building preserves as much contiguous open space in the park as possible.
The slightly angular volume gives the northwest area a precise urban setting.
The main uses and associated infrastructures are sensibly arranged for functional and operational processes.
The restaurant and outdoor terrace are in a desirable location and form a beautiful dialogue with the pool.
The facade is attractive in its combinatorics, tectonics, and location-specific material character.
The park is respected, the architecture is withdrawn, and the degree of sealing is low.
The project achieves good compactness and a remarkably small footprint.
The concept is recognized as preserving substantial park space with a compact peripheral building.

negative.statement: Stacking the uses creates additional effort and loses operational synergy.
The external ice-rink enclosure is unresolved, and future energy and climatic needs were overlooked.
The large external staircase lacks sufficient architectural design power.
The necessary roof housing is not convincing.
A more spatially attractive route to the ice-rink grandstand would be desirable.
The terrace additions are architecturally unsightly and obscure the material expression.
The newly acquired lounge area is too open in front of the unconvincing ramp staircase.
The arrangement of uses has functional and operational deficiencies.
The deep basement produces a large excavation volume.
The carrying concept is unconvincing and the construction method is resource-intensive.
The stacked arrangement creates thermal neighbourhoods that disrupt efficient operation and energy performance.
The project cannot be implemented in several independent stages.
